title: StepSafe: Learning Timely Intervention with Context-Aware Safety Reasoning
abstract: arXiv:2610.20960v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Safety in agentic systems is inherently sequential: whether an action is safe depends on prior actions, tool outputs, information disclosures, and interactions among agents. Recent work has shifted agent safety guardrails from post-hoc trajectory-level assessment toward step-level action diagnosis and proactive risk prediction, yet existing training objectives provide limited supervision for how step evidence accumulates over time and when it becomes sufficient to justify intervention. We propose \methodlong~(ASPO): a training framework for step-level timely intervention. Pre-fix level stage alignment allows crediting each decision at its own step: it compares each response with the other responses sampled at the same prefix and rewards the action that fits the stage, continuing before the risk is visible, asking while clarification can still avert harm, and stopping before harm is irreversible. translated_title: StepSafe：通过情境感知安全推理学习及时干预
translated_abstract: 智能体系统的安全性本质上是序列性的：一个动作是否安全取决于先前的动作、工具输出、信息披露以及智能体之间的交互。最近的研究已将智能体安全防护机制从事后的轨迹级评估转向步骤级的动作诊断和主动风险预测，然而现有的训练目标对于步骤证据如何随时间累积、以及何时才足以支撑干预这一问题上提供的监督十分有限。我们提出StepSafe（ASPO）：一个面向步骤级及时干预的训练框架。前缀级阶段对齐使每个决策能在其所在步骤获得相应的信用：它将每个响应与在同一前缀下采样的其他响应进行比较，并奖励符合当前阶段的动作——在风险尚未显现之前继续推进，在澄清仍能避免伤害时进行询问，在伤害变得不可逆转之前及时停止。自适应反馈自蒸馏进一步……
tldr: StepSafe提出了一种步骤级及时干预训练框架，通过前缀级阶段对齐与自适应反馈自蒸馏，使智能体能够根据逐步累积的证据在恰当的时机选择继续、询问或停止，从而实现情境感知的安全防护。
en_tdlr: StepSafe is a training framework for step-level timely intervention that uses prefix-level stage alignment and adaptive feedback self-distillation to teach agents when to continue, ask for clarification, or stop, based on how safety evidence accumulates across sequential actions.
